tools.name: finalize_site
tools.description: Promote a pending ATTIM site version to live. Anonymous sites require claimToken.

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Delete an owned ATTIM site, or an anonymous site when claimToken is supplied.

tools.name: rename_site
tools.description: Rename an owned ATTIM site by changing its slug. Requires a paid (Hobby or Team) account; the previous slug redirects to the new one for a grace period.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List ATTIM sites owned by the authenticated account.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: List the latest 10 retained finalized versions of an owned ATTIM project, including names and the current version ID. Team viewers can read history.

tools.name: rename_version
tools.description: Set or clear the name of a retained finalized project version. Pass null to clear. Requires project write access.

tools.name: preview_version
tools.description: Create a private one-use preview link for a retained finalized project version. Open it within 60 seconds; the session lasts 15 minutes.

tools.name: download_version
tools.description: Get an authenticated MCP resource link to a retained project version ZIP. Read it with resources/read using the same account credentials.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Copy a retained project version into a new live version. Requires write access and the current version ID from list_versions to prevent stale restores.

tools.name: set_variables
tools.description: Set public variables for an owned ATTIM site. Array entries can include a friendly label without changing their technical placement key.

tools.name: set_password_protection
tools.description: Enable, update, or disable password protection for an owned site. A grandfathered anonymous protected site may be updated or disabled with its claimToken; new anonymous protection cannot be enabled.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "create_profile" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_site, create_profile, get_public_profile, get_link_page_template, get_profile · Private data: publish_site, update_site, read_site, edit_site, preview_version, download_version, set_password_protection · Public sink: publish_site, claim_site, update_site, get_public_profile, set_links, get_link_page_template, get_profile · Destructive: edit_site, delete_site.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_site, create_profile, get_public_profile, get_link_page_template, get_profile · Private data: publish_site, update_site, read_site, edit_site, preview_version, download_version, set_password_protection · Public sink: publish_site, claim_site, update_site, get_public_profile, set_links, get_link_page_template, get_profile · Destructive: edit_site, delete_site

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
